pointers.sentence: `BaseSpatialField`, a `django.db.models.Field`, and the classes built on it answer them: `GeometryField`, for vector geometries, and `RasterField`, for grids of values (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField`).

Where `django.db.models.Field.db_type` looks the internal type up in the backend's table of column types ([A field: the base class](../models/fields.md)), `BaseSpatialField.db_type` returns what the connection's operations object writes with `geo_db_type` (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.db_type`).
PostGIS's writes the field's geometry type, with `"Z"` for three dimensions, and its SRID (`django/contrib/gis/db/backends/postgis/operations.py:PostGISOperations.geo_db_type`).

That argument stands in for `db_index` because a spatial index, the documentation says, is typically a variant of the R-tree (`docs/ref/contrib/gis/model-api.txt`); the backend's schema editor makes it ([Spatial backends: PostGIS, SpatiaLite, MySQL and Oracle](spatial-backends.md)).

`BaseSpatialField.geodetic`, `BaseSpatialField.units_name` and their siblings ask `get_srid_info`, which the first time reads the SRID's row of `"spatial_ref_sys"`, or Oracle's `"CS_SRS"`, and keeps its units, its spheroid and whether it is geographic in `_srid_cache`, by alias and SRID, for the life of the process; on MySQL, whose backend has no model of such a table, GDAL's `SpatialReference` answers (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:get_srid_info`).
`GeometryField.contribute_to_class` puts a `SpatialProxy` on the model class under the field's attname (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:GeometryField.contribute_to_class`).

`SpatialProxy.__get__` parses a string or a `memoryview` at the first read, with `GEOSGeometry` and the field's `max_geom_collections`, and assigns the result back through `__set__`, so the string is parsed once and its type checked then (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/proxy.py:SpatialProxy`).

`BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`, which a lookup calls when it is made, keeps a `GEOSGeometry` or a `GDALRaster`, makes a geometry of a string, and of bytes a raster if GDAL can read one or else a geometry; then `BaseSpatialField.get_srid` gives a value with no SRID, or with -1, the field's, and keeps any other unless the field's is -1 (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`).

`BaseSpatialField.get_placeholder_sql` hands the compiler's question, what to write where the value goes, to the backend's `get_geom_placeholder_sql`, which on PostGIS transforms a value of another SRID (`django/contrib/gis/db/backends/postgis/operations.py:PostGISOperations.get_geom_placeholder_sql`).

So `GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value` refuses a dictionary, a string or a path with `DisallowedRasterLookup`, a `SuspiciousOperation`, which a request answers with 400 (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value`) ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md)).

For a string the refusal waits while `GEOSGeometry` has its turn, so WKT still works; it is raised if that fails on a string that begins "/vsi" or looks like JSON, as a filter of moorings by "/vsicurl/https://charts.example/harbour.tif" did (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`).

On the way out a geometry field has no `from_db_value`: the backend adds a converter for every expression whose output field is a geometry field (`django/contrib/gis/db/backends/base/operations.py:BaseSpatialOperations.get_db_converters`).

PostGIS's reads the WKB and gives the result the field's `geom_class` without asking GEOS its type; for `GeometryField`, whose `geom_class` is `None`, it asks (`django/contrib/gis/db/backends/postgis/operations.py:PostGISOperations.get_geometry_converter`).
`max_geom_collections`, 198 by default, limits the nesting of geometry collections in WKT and their number in WKB, against a crash in GEOS the release notes describe (`docs/releases/6.0.8.txt`).

`PointField`, `LineStringField`, `PolygonField`, `MultiPointField`, `MultiLineStringField`, `MultiPolygonField` and `GeometryCollectionField`, the subclasses of `GeometryField`, set three class attributes and a description (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:PointField`): `GeometryField.geom_type`, the type's OpenGIS name, which PostGIS and MySQL write into the column's type; `GeometryField.geom_class`, the GEOS class the proxy demands and the converter makes; and `GeometryField.form_class`, the form field of the same name.

The lookups, and some functions that serve as transforms, are registered on `BaseSpatialField` itself when `django.contrib.gis.db.models` is imported (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/lookups.py`, `django/contrib/gis/db/models/functions.py`); `"exact"` is another name for `"same_as"`, which PostGIS writes as `~=` ([Spatial lookups, functions and distances](spatial-queries.md)).

The lookups, and some functions that serve as transforms, are registered on `BaseSpatialField` itself when `django.contrib.gis.db.models` is imported (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/lookups.py`, `django/contrib/gis/db/models/functions.py`); `"exact"` is another name for `"same_as"`, which PostGIS writes as `~=` ([Spatial lookups, functions and distances](spatial-queries.md)).
`ExtentField` is no model's field but the output field of the aggregates `Extent` and `Extent3D` (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:ExtentField`).
